definitions.gloss: tide; tidal phenomenon; the rise and fall of sea levels
definitions.explanation: The periodic rising and falling of sea levels caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and sun. A technical term used in oceanography and navigation.

examples.japanese: {潮汐|ちょうせき}の{変化|へんか}を{観測|かんそく}する。
{潮汐|ちょうせき}は{月|つき}の{引力|いんりょく}によって{起|お}こる。
examples.english: Tides are caused by the gravitational pull of the moon.

examples.japanese: {漁師|りょうし}は{潮汐|ちょうせき}の{動|うご}きを{知|し}ることが{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: For fishermen, knowing the tidal movements is essential.

notes:
Composed of {潮|ちょう} (high tide) and {汐|せき} (low tide). The technical and scientific term for the tidal phenomenon — the periodic rise and fall of the sea caused by gravitational forces of the moon and sun. Used in oceanography, fishing, navigation, and weather contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {潮汐|ちょうせき}{表|ひょう}: tide table
- {潮汐|ちょうせき}{力|りょく}: tidal force
- {潮汐|ちょうせき}{現象|げんしょう}: tidal phenomenon
- {潮汐|ちょうせき}{発電|はつでん}: tidal power generation
- {潮汐|ちょうせき}の{差|さ}: tidal range

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {潮|しお}: tide — more general and colloquial; also means salt water or sea current
- {干潮|かんちょう}: low tide — the specific state of low water
- {満潮|まんちょう}: high tide — the specific state of high water
- {潮|しお}の{満|み}ち{引|ひ}き: ebb and flow — more literary or poetic expression
